Pin the three-way interaction effect of a design with two moderators

Source: R/aie3.R
set_aie3.Rd

For a design built with ape_dgp(moderator = , moderator2 = ), solves all seven effect coefficients from targets in probability points. The pinned estimand is the three-way average interaction effect (as in the ginteff package): the two-way average interaction effect of the focal variable and the moderator when the second moderator is set to 1 for everyone, minus the same when it is set to 0, each averaged over the covariates. With three binary variables this is the triple difference of the eight counterfactual cell rates. The effect is symmetric in its three variables.

Usage

set_aie3(dgp, target, main, two_way)

Arguments

dgp

A powerape_dgp from ape_dgp() with a moderator and a moderator2.

target

Assumed true three-way average interaction effect (the planning value), in probability points.

main

Numeric vector of three: the main-effect anchors (focal, moderator, second moderator).

two_way

Numeric vector of three: the two-way anchors (focal x moderator, focal x second moderator, moderator x second moderator).

Value

The dgp with all effect coefficients and target_est filled in; estimand becomes "aie3".

Details

All anchors are explicit; there are no silent defaults:

  • main: the average partial effect of each variable with the other two held at their reference values (0 for binary, the mean for continuous), in the order focal, moderator, second moderator.

  • two_way: the two-way average interaction effect of each pair with the third variable held at its reference value (not averaged over it), in the order focal x moderator, focal x second moderator, moderator x second moderator.

  • target: the three-way effect. The focal-by-moderator effect is two_way[1] when the second moderator is 0 and two_way[1] + target when it is 1.

A two-way anchor of 0 says that the pair does not interact in probability points when the third variable is at its reference value. It does not say that the product's coefficient is 0: in a probit or logit, main effects alone produce interaction effects on the probability scale, of every order. Errors report the attainable range when a target is infeasible.

Three-way designs run through ape_power(), ape_curve(), ape_n() and ape_mde() (which searches the three-way effect and holds the six other anchors), under the index analysis or, with set_analysis(), a linear probability analysis whose estimate is the coefficient of the triple product. A three-way effect is expensive: with balanced binary variables and the same effect in probability points, each interaction order needs about four times the observations of the order below.

Computing time

A design with three binary variables and no covariates is pinned at once. With covariates the anchors are integrals over the covariate distribution, and at the default integration size of ape_dgp() (n_int = 4e5) pinning takes about 15 seconds with three binary variables, about 40 seconds when the focal variable or the moderator is continuous, and about a minute when both are (effects of continuous variables level off as their coefficient grows, so their coefficients are found by a grid scan). ape_mde() solves only the triple product's coefficient again at each candidate effect (about 10 seconds with a continuous variable). A smaller n_int speeds up exploration.

Examples

d <- ape_dgp(focal = pa_var("treat", "binary", p = 0.5),
             moderator = pa_var("female", "binary", p = 0.5),
             moderator2 = pa_var("public", "binary", p = 0.5),
             baseline = 0.30)
d <- set_aie3(d, target = 0.10, main = c(0.08, 0.04, 0.02),
              two_way = c(0.03, 0, 0))
d
#> powerape DGP -- probit
#>   focal: treat (binary, p = 0.50)
#>   moderator: female (binary, p = 0.50)
#>   second moderator: public (binary, p = 0.50) (all pairwise products and the triple product included)
#>   covariates: none
#>   baseline P(Y=1 | reference) = 0.300, nuisance signal (latent pseudo-R2) = 0.000
#>   true three-way AIE (treat x female x public) pinned at +0.1000 (beta = 0.2526)
#>   main APEs at reference: treat +0.080, female +0.040, public +0.020
#>   two-way AIEs with the third variable at reference: treat x female +0.030, treat x public +0.000, female x public +0.000
#>   cell rates P(Y=1 | treat, female, public): 000 0.300 | 100 0.380 | 010 0.340 | 110 0.450 | 001 0.320 | 101 0.400 | 011 0.360 | 111 0.570
true_aie3(d)
#> [1] 0.1
